The Integrations screen works with no config at all — sources, consumers and
last-used come from agent configs and real call history. This file supplies
only the three things no log can state:
label            what a person calls the source, where the raw key is opaque
expected_interval how often a grant SHOULD run. Without it nothing can be
called stale, so a daily job that died six days ago looks
exactly like one that ran this morning.
capabilities[] splits one source's traffic into scope classes by matching the
bare tool name (no mcp__<server>__ prefix). This is what makes the security
model readable: with it, Gmail shows that exactly one consumer sends mail.
Anything found in the logs but absent here still displays, under its raw
identifiers. A grant listed here but never seen in the logs displays as
'never used' — usually dead weight or a credential issued and forgotten.
Consumer keys are session sources as the gateway records them (api_server,
cron, tui, telegram, webui, cli) or, for workflow pipelines, the name passed
